simple: the file system is still correct, or can be made correct, whenever the power is cut.
analogy: the catalogue never sends a pupil to the wrong book, even after a power cut in the middle of shelving.
precise: the property that every on-disk state reachable by a crash at any point (with any subset of unflushed writes lost) satisfies the file system's invariants after the defined recovery step, and that every operation acknowledged as durable is preserved.
source: D1 of F3-43 (Remzi H. Arpaci-Dusseau, Andrea C. Arpaci-Dusseau, "Operating Systems: Three Easy Pieces") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: memory inside the disk that holds writes for a while before they reach the medium; it forgets everything when the power goes.
analogy: the porter's trolley in the corridor: books on it are not yet on any shelf.
precise: a device-side buffer that may acknowledge a write before the data is on non-volatile media and may write cached blocks to the media in any order.
source: D7 of F3-43 (NVM Express, "NVM Express Base Specification") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a command that tells the disk "put everything you are holding onto the medium, and tell me when it is done".
analogy: the porter's signed delivery note: everything on the trolley is now on a shelf.
precise: a device command (NVMe Flush, ATA FLUSH CACHE EXT, SCSI SYNCHRONIZE CACHE, virtio-blk flush request) that completes only after all previously completed writes are on non-volatile media.
source: D7 of F3-43 (NVM Express, "NVM Express Base Specification"); D8 of F3-43 (INCITS T13, "ATA/ATAPI Command Set" (FLUSH CACHE EXT, write commands with FUA, IDENTIFY DEVICE cache bits), and INCITS T10, "SCSI Block Commands" (SYNCHRONIZE CACHE, FUA)); D9 of F3-43 (OASIS, "Virtual I/O Device (VIRTIO) Specification") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a flag on one write that says "do not finish this until it is on the medium".
analogy: carrying one book to the shelf yourself instead of putting it on the trolley.
precise: a per-command attribute of a write that makes its completion imply that this command's data is on non-volatile media; it says nothing about other writes still in the cache.
source: D7 of F3-43 (NVM Express, "NVM Express Base Specification"); D8 of F3-43 (INCITS T13, "ATA/ATAPI Command Set" (FLUSH CACHE EXT, write commands with FUA, IDENTIFY DEVICE cache bits), and INCITS T10, "SCSI Block Commands" (SYNCHRONIZE CACHE, FUA)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: one possible picture of the disk after a power cut.
analogy: which books happened to reach their shelves when the lights went out.
precise: the media contents given a cut after operation k: every write before the last completed flush is present, and any subset of the writes issued after it may be present.
source: D1 of F3-43 (Remzi H. Arpaci-Dusseau, Andrea C. Arpaci-Dusseau, "Operating Systems: Three Easy Pieces") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a program that reads the whole file system after a crash and repairs what it can.
analogy: a librarian who walks every shelf with the catalogue and fixes the cards.
precise: an offline tool that verifies cross-structure invariants (bitmaps against pointers, link counts against directory entries) and repairs violations; its run time grows with the size of the file system, and it cannot know which of two contradicting versions the user meant.
source: D1 of F3-43 (Remzi H. Arpaci-Dusseau, Andrea C. Arpaci-Dusseau, "Operating Systems: Three Easy Pieces") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: first write down what you are about to change in a separate log, mark it complete, and only then change the real places.
analogy: the librarian's day book: "atlas to shelf 12, card updated, chart updated", ticked off before she starts.
precise: recording a transaction's new block images (physical journaling) or operations (logical journaling) in a log, followed by a commit record; after a crash, committed transactions are replayed and uncommitted ones ignored.
source: D1 of F3-43 (Remzi H. Arpaci-Dusseau, Andrea C. Arpaci-Dusseau, "Operating Systems: Three Easy Pieces"); D2 of F3-43 (Stephen C. Tweedie, "Journaling the Linux ext2fs Filesystem") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: only metadata goes into the journal, but file data is written to its final place before the metadata that points to it is committed.
analogy: the atlas is on the shelf before the day book's entry about its card is ticked.
precise: the ext3/ext4 default journaling mode: data blocks of a transaction are forced to disk before its commit record, so committed metadata never points to unwritten data.
source: D11 of F3-43 (The Linux kernel documentation) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: keep the disk consistent by tracking which writes depend on which, and writing them in a safe order.
analogy: the atlas first, then the chart, then the card, every time.
precise: a technique that records dependencies between cached metadata blocks and orders (and if needed rolls back) updates so that the on-disk image only ever contains leaks, never dangling pointers.
source: D3 of F3-43 (Marshall Kirk McKusick, Gregory R. Ganger, "Soft Updates: A Technique for Eliminating Most Synchronous Writes in the Fast Filesystem" (USENIX 1999)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: never change a block in place; write a new copy and switch one pointer at the end.
analogy: write a whole new catalogue drawer, then swap the label on the cabinet.
precise: an update discipline in which modified blocks are written to free space and the tree of pointers above them is rewritten up to a root, which is updated with a single atomic write after a flush.
source: D1 of F3-43 (Remzi H. Arpaci-Dusseau, Andrea C. Arpaci-Dusseau, "Operating Systems: Three Easy Pieces") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the system call a program uses to ask "make this file safe on disk now".
analogy: asking the librarian to confirm that this one book, card and chart are done.
precise: a POSIX call that returns after the file's data and the metadata needed to retrieve it have been transferred to the storage device; whether the directory entry naming the file is included is not guaranteed by POSIX, hence the separate directory fsync.
source: D10 of F3-43 (IEEE and The Open Group, "The Open Group Base Specifications" (POSIX.1)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a write that was cut in half by a power failure, leaving part old and part new.
analogy: half of a catalogue card rewritten.
precise: a multi-sector write of which only some sectors reached the media; devices guarantee atomicity only up to a documented unit, often one logical block.
source: D7 of F3-43 (NVM Express, "NVM Express Base Specification") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a recording of every block a file system wrote and every flush it asked for, in order.
analogy: the porter's list of everything he carried, with the signed lines.
precise: a log of (block number, block contents) write records and flush records taken at the block-device interface; together with the starting image it determines every crash state.
source: D5 of F3-44 (Jayashree Mohan et al., "Finding Crash-Consistency Bugs with Bounded Black-Box Crash Testing" (OSDI 2018)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a test program that fakes many power failures and checks the disk after each one.
analogy: replaying the porter's list to a random point, 500 times, with an inspector after each replay.
precise: a test that builds crash images (by replaying a write stream with unflushed writes randomly dropped, or by killing an emulator), runs recovery and an independent checker, and verifies the application-level promises.
source: D5 of F3-44 (Jayashree Mohan et al., "Finding Crash-Consistency Bugs with Bounded Black-Box Crash Testing" (OSDI 2018)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a block that holds no file data, only a list of block numbers of the file.
analogy: an index card that lists more shelf places for a very long book series.
precise: in ext2, inode pointers 12, 13 and 14 point to single, double and triple indirect blocks, each holding block-size/4 32-bit block numbers.
source: D1 of F3-44 (Dave Poirier, "The Second Extended File System: Internal Layout") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a file with ranges that were never written and take no disk space; they read as zeros.
analogy: a numbered series with empty places that are not reserved on any shelf.
precise: logical blocks whose pointer is 0; reads return zeros, and i_blocks counts only allocated blocks (including indirect blocks), in 512-byte units.
source: D1 of F3-44 (Dave Poirier, "The Second Extended File System: Internal Layout") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a second name for the same file.
analogy: two catalogue cards for one book.
precise: a directory entry pointing to an existing inode; the inode's i_links_count counts its names, and the inode is freed when the count reaches 0 (and no process holds it open).
source: D1 of F3-44 (Dave Poirier, "The Second Extended File System: Internal Layout") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a small file whose content is a path to another file, stored inside the inode itself.
analogy: a card that says "see the card for the atlas".
precise: an ext2 symlink whose target (under 60 bytes) is stored in the inode's block-pointer area instead of a data block, with i_blocks = 0.
source: D1 of F3-44 (Dave Poirier, "The Second Extended File System: Internal Layout") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a file that exists on disk but has no name in any directory.
analogy: a book on a shelf with no card anywhere.
precise: an inode with a non-zero link count and no directory entry; e2fsck reports it as "Unattached inode" and offers to connect it to lost+found.
source: D2 of F3-44 (e2fsprogs manual pages e2fsck(8) and debugfs(8)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the kinds of checker complaints your design allows after a crash, written down before testing.
analogy: "a free place marked taken is fine; a card pointing to the wrong book is not".
precise: the categories, declared in the FS1 plan, of e2fsck findings that do not lose, mix or expose data: leaked blocks and inodes, counters, link counts and i_blocks too high.
source: D1 of F3-44 (Dave Poirier, "The Second Extended File System: Internal Layout") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a note in the recording that says "the program was told this file is safe".
analogy: the librarian's signature under one move.
precise: a record appended to the write stream after an fsync returned, naming the file and its expected contents; the harness checks every promise issued before the cut.
source: D1 of F3-44 (Dave Poirier, "The Second Extended File System: Internal Layout") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the journal format and code that ext3 and ext4 use on Linux.
analogy: the day book's standard layout, so any librarian can read it.
precise: Journaling Block Device version 2, Linux's generic block-level journal layer; its on-disk format (inside an ext3/ext4 file system, usually in inode 8) is shared by the kernel and by e2fsprogs.
source: D1 of F3-45 (The Linux kernel documentation, "ext4 Data Structures and Algorithms") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the first block of the journal, saying how big it is and where the log currently starts.
analogy: the day book's cover page with a bookmark.
precise: a block with the JBD2 magic number, block type 3 or 4 (v1/v2), journal block size and length, the first usable log block, the sequence number expected next (s_sequence) and the log start (s_start, 0 meaning the log is empty), plus feature flags and a UUID.
source: D1 of F3-45 (The Linux kernel documentation, "ext4 Data Structures and Algorithms") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a journal block that lists which file-system blocks the following log blocks are copies of.
analogy: the line in the day book that says "next pages: card 12, chart page 3".
precise: a block of type 1 with the transaction's sequence number, followed by tags; each tag holds a target block number and flags (escaped, same UUID, last tag), and the first tag carries a 16-byte UUID.
source: D1 of F3-45 (The Linux kernel documentation, "ext4 Data Structures and Algorithms") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the block that says "this transaction is complete".
analogy: the tick under a finished entry.
precise: a block of type 2 with the transaction's sequence number (and optionally a checksum and a time stamp); recovery replays a transaction only if its commit block is found.
source: D1 of F3-45 (The Linux kernel documentation, "ext4 Data Structures and Algorithms") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a note in the journal that says "do not replay older copies of these blocks".
analogy: "ignore earlier entries about card 12: that card was thrown away and the slot reused".
precise: a block of type 5 listing block numbers; during replay, a logged copy of a listed block from a transaction with a sequence number not later than the revoke's is skipped, so a block freed and reused for data is not overwritten by stale metadata.
source: D1 of F3-45 (The Linux kernel documentation, "ext4 Data Structures and Algorithms") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: hiding a data block that happens to look like a journal block, so recovery does not mistake it.
analogy: crossing out a tick that appears by accident on a copied page.
precise: if a logged block begins with the JBD2 magic number, its first four bytes are written as zero and its tag gets the escape flag; replay restores the magic number.
source: D1 of F3-45 (The Linux kernel documentation, "ext4 Data Structures and Algorithms") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: writing the journaled blocks to their real places, after which their space in the journal can be reused.
analogy: copying the day book's pages onto the real cards and then turning the page.
precise: writing a committed transaction's blocks in place, making them durable, and then advancing s_start (or setting it to 0) in the journal superblock so that recovery no longer needs that part of the log.
source: D2 of F3-45 (Stephen C. Tweedie, "Journaling the Linux ext2fs Filesystem") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: after a crash, redoing every complete transaction from the journal.
analogy: copying every ticked entry onto the cards again.
precise: scanning the log from s_start for blocks with the expected sequence numbers, collecting transactions that end in a commit block, applying revokes, writing the logged copies to their targets, flushing, and marking the log empty; it is idempotent.
source: D1 of F3-45 (The Linux kernel documentation, "ext4 Data Structures and Algorithms") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a flag in the file system's superblock that says "the journal may hold work that has not been replayed".
analogy: a sign on the desk: "read the day book before opening".
precise: the ext3/ext4 incompatible feature flag (0x4) set while the file system is mounted with a journal and cleared after a clean unmount or a replay; tools that cannot replay must refuse to mount.
source: D1 of F3-45 (The Linux kernel documentation, "ext4 Data Structures and Algorithms") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: three sets of switches in the superblock that say which extensions the file system uses.
analogy: notes on the library door: "you may ignore this", "you must understand this to read", "you may read but not write".
precise: bit masks at fixed superblock offsets; an unknown incompatible bit forbids mounting, an unknown read-only compatible bit forbids writing, an unknown compatible bit may be ignored.
source: D1 of F3-46 (The Linux kernel documentation, "ext4 Data Structures and Algorithms") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: one entry saying "these many consecutive blocks of the file are stored at these consecutive places on the disk".
analogy: "shelf 12, places 4 to 40" on one card.
precise: a 12-byte leaf entry: first logical block (32 bits), length (16 bits, above 32,768 meaning uninitialised), physical start (48 bits).
source: D1 of F3-46 (The Linux kernel documentation, "ext4 Data Structures and Algorithms") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the small tree of extents that maps a whole file; tiny files keep it inside the inode.
analogy: the index card that points to a few range cards.
precise: a B-tree whose root (a 12-byte header and up to four entries) occupies the inode's 60-byte i_block; index entries point to tree blocks, each with a header, entries and (with metadata checksums) a 4-byte tail checksum.
source: D1 of F3-46 (The Linux kernel documentation, "ext4 Data Structures and Algorithms") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: space reserved for a file but never written; it must read as zeros.
analogy: shelf places reserved for a series that has not arrived.
precise: an extent whose length field exceeds 32,768 (the length is the value minus 32,768); used by preallocation, read as zeros until converted.
source: D1 of F3-46 (The Linux kernel documentation, "ext4 Data Structures and Algorithms") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the bitmaps and inode tables of several block groups are placed together.
analogy: the charts of several floors kept on one desk.
precise: an incompatible feature that lets a group's metadata live outside the group, so readers must take every location from the group descriptor, never compute it.
source: D1 of F3-46 (The Linux kernel documentation, "ext4 Data Structures and Algorithms") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: block numbers get 48 or 64 bits, and group descriptors grow to hold them.
analogy: longer shelf numbers for a bigger library.
precise: the 64bit incompatible feature: group descriptors of s_desc_size bytes (64 in this build) with high halves of each block field, and a 64-bit block count.
source: D1 of F3-46 (The Linux kernel documentation, "ext4 Data Structures and Algorithms") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a large directory with an index that sends each name, by a number computed from it, to one block.
analogy: the rule that turns a name into a drawer number.
precise: a directory whose first block holds a dx_root (disguised as entries for . and ..) with sorted (hash, block) pairs, optional dx_node levels, and ordinary leaf blocks; the hash (here half-MD4 with a seed from the superblock) selects the leaf.
source: D1 of F3-46 (The Linux kernel documentation, "ext4 Data Structures and Algorithms") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a 32-bit check code computed over each metadata structure.
analogy: the seal on each drawer.
precise: the Castagnoli CRC-32 used by ext4's metadata_csum feature, seeded per file system from the UUID (or a stored seed) and per object from numbers such as the inode number and generation; stored in the superblock, descriptors (16 bits), inodes, extent and directory block tails.
source: D1 of F3-46 (The Linux kernel documentation, "ext4 Data Structures and Algorithms") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a very small file stored inside its inode instead of in a block.
analogy: a short note written on the catalogue card itself.
precise: the inline_data incompatible feature: file (or directory) contents in i_block and an extended attribute; FS3's goal lists it, and this chapter's reader refuses it.
source: D1 of F3-46 (The Linux kernel documentation, "ext4 Data Structures and Algorithms") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the file system on large SD cards, camera cards and USB sticks.
analogy: a newer catalogue for big collections, related to the old FAT catalogue.
precise: Microsoft's Extended File Allocation Table file system, with a 32-bit FAT, an allocation bitmap, 64-bit file sizes, directory entry sets with checksums and an up-case table; its specification was published by Microsoft.
source: D1 of F3-47 (Microsoft, "exFAT file system specification") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the first twelve sectors, describing the volume, followed by an identical backup.
analogy: the library's front door notice, with a copy at the back door.
precise: the main boot sector, eight extended boot sectors, an OEM parameters sector, a reserved sector and a boot checksum sector (a 32-bit checksum of sectors 0–10 repeated to fill sector 11); sectors 12–23 hold the backup.
source: D1 of F3-47 (Microsoft, "exFAT file system specification") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the part of the volume where file contents and directories live, in clusters.
analogy: the shelves.
precise: the region starting at ClusterHeapOffset, divided into ClusterCount clusters numbered from 2.
source: D1 of F3-47 (Microsoft, "exFAT file system specification") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: one bit per cluster: used or free.
analogy: the free-place chart.
precise: a file in the cluster heap, described by a root-directory entry of type 0x81, whose bit n − 2 says whether cluster n is allocated; in exFAT it, not the FAT, is the authority on free space.
source: D1 of F3-47 (Microsoft, "exFAT file system specification") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a table that says what each character looks like in capitals, so that names can be compared without case.
analogy: the rule that "atlas" and "ATLAS" are the same card.
precise: a file (root entry type 0x82, with a checksum of its contents) mapping UTF-16 code units to their upper-case forms; used for case-insensitive name comparison and for the name hash.
source: D1 of F3-47 (Microsoft, "exFAT file system specification") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the group of 32-byte entries that together describe one file.
analogy: one catalogue card made of several slips stapled together, with a check number on the first slip.
precise: a File entry (0x85: secondary count, set checksum, attributes, times), a Stream Extension entry (0xC0: flags, name length, name hash, valid data length, first cluster, data length) and 1–17 File Name entries (0xC1: 15 UTF-16 code units each).
source: D1 of F3-47 (Microsoft, "exFAT file system specification") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a flag that says "this file's clusters are all next to each other; do not look in the FAT".
analogy: "all volumes stand side by side from place 5".
precise: bit 1 of the Stream Extension's general secondary flags; when set, the clusters are FirstCluster to FirstCluster + ⌈DataLength / cluster size⌉ − 1 and the FAT entries are undefined and must not be used.
source: D1 of F3-47 (Microsoft, "exFAT file system specification") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: how much of a file has really been written; the rest reads as zeros.
analogy: reserved shelf places that are still empty.
precise: the Stream Extension's ValidDataLength, at most DataLength; bytes beyond it are undefined on disk and must read as zero.
source: D1 of F3-47 (Microsoft, "exFAT file system specification") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the file system of CDs, DVDs and ".iso" files.
analogy: the printed and bound catalogue.
precise: the file structure standardised as ECMA-119 / ISO 9660: 2,048-byte logical sectors, a volume descriptor set from sector 16, directories as lists of variable-length records, each file as one contiguous extent (in the basic levels).
source: D1 of F3-48 (Ecma International, ECMA-119 "Volume and File Structure of CDROM for Information Interchange") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a 2,048-byte sector that describes one view of the disc.
analogy: the title page.
precise: a sector starting with a type byte and "CD001": type 1 primary, 2 supplementary (Joliet), 0 boot record (El Torito), 255 set terminator.
source: D1 of F3-48 (Ecma International, ECMA-119 "Volume and File Structure of CDROM for Information Interchange") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a list of every directory and its parent, so that a reader can find a deep directory without walking.
analogy: the book's table of contents.
precise: a table of directory identifiers, extents and parent numbers in breadth-first order, stored once little-endian (L) and once big-endian (M).
source: D1 of F3-48 (Ecma International, ECMA-119 "Volume and File Structure of CDROM for Information Interchange") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a number written twice, once for each kind of computer.
analogy: a page number printed in two scripts.
precise: ISO 9660's 16- and 32-bit fields stored little-endian then big-endian, so either kind of machine reads its half directly.
source: D1 of F3-48 (Ecma International, ECMA-119 "Volume and File Structure of CDROM for Information Interchange") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: notes added to each directory record giving the POSIX name, permissions and link target.
analogy: margin notes for readers who want the full details.
precise: the System Use Sharing Protocol defines tagged entries in a record's System Use area (SP, CE, ER, ...); the Rock Ridge Interchange Protocol defines PX (mode, links, uid, gid), NM (name), SL (symbolic link), TF (times) and others.
source: D3 of F3-48 (IEEE P1281 "System Use Sharing Protocol" and P1282 "Rock Ridge Interchange Protocol" drafts) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a second directory tree with Unicode names, for Windows.
analogy: a translated index.
precise: a supplementary volume descriptor with an escape sequence (%/@, %/C or %/E for UCS-2 levels 1–3) whose root leads to a separate tree of records with UCS-2 big-endian identifiers, pointing at the same file extents.
source: D2 of F3-48 (Microsoft, "Joliet Specification") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the rules for making a CD bootable.
analogy: the caretaker's "start here" page.
precise: a boot record volume descriptor pointing at a boot catalog: a validation entry with a checksum, a default entry, and optional section headers and entries for other platforms (0xEF for UEFI).
source: D4 of F3-48 (Phoenix Technologies and IBM, "El Torito Bootable CD-ROM Format Specification" version 1.0) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the BIOS loads a small program from the CD and runs it, without pretending the CD is a floppy or hard disk.
analogy: "run the program on page 73 as it is".
precise: media type 0 in a catalog entry: the BIOS loads sector count 512-byte virtual sectors from the given 2,048-byte load RBA to the load segment (default 0x7C0) and jumps to it with DL = the drive number.
source: D4 of F3-48 (Phoenix Technologies and IBM, "El Torito Bootable CD-ROM Format Specification" version 1.0) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: Windows's main file system.
analogy: the neighbouring school's library, rules unpublished.
precise: the New Technology File System, in which all metadata, including the allocation bitmap and the MFT itself, is stored as files described by MFT records; Microsoft has not published an on-disk specification, and the structures used here come from reverse-engineering documentation.
source: D1 of F3-49 (Linux-NTFS project, "NTFS Documentation" (Richard Russon and Yuval Fledel)); D2 of F3-49 (Brian Carrier, "File System Forensic Analysis", NTFS chapters) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a table with one fixed-size record per file and directory.
analogy: the master register.
precise: the file $MFT (record 0), whose records (commonly 1 KiB) start with "FILE"; records 0–15 are system files ($MFT, $MFTMirr, $LogFile, $Volume, $AttrDef, the root "." at 5, $Bitmap, $Boot, ...).
source: D1 of F3-49 (Linux-NTFS project, "NTFS Documentation" (Richard Russon and Yuval Fledel)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: one piece of a file's description, such as its name or its contents, stored in the record or out on the disk.
analogy: a section of the form; a short one is written on the form, a long one says which shelves hold it.
precise: a typed, optionally named record part (0x10 standard information, 0x30 file name, 0x80 data, 0x90 index root, 0xA0 index allocation, 0xB0 bitmap, ...); a resident attribute holds its value in the record; a non-resident one holds a run list and sizes.
source: D1 of F3-49 (Linux-NTFS project, "NTFS Documentation" (Richard Russon and Yuval Fledel)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a compact list of "this many clusters, starting there".
analogy: shelf ranges written as "3 places from shelf 62, then 3 from three shelves back".
precise: mapping pairs: a header byte whose low nibble is the length field's size and high nibble the offset field's size; the offset is signed and relative to the previous run; an offset size of 0 is a sparse run; a 0 header ends the list.
source: D1 of F3-49 (Linux-NTFS project, "NTFS Documentation" (Richard Russon and Yuval Fledel)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a check that every 512-byte piece of a record was written at the same time.
analogy: the form number at the foot of every page.
precise: before writing, the last two bytes of each 512-byte stride of a record or index block are saved in the update sequence array and replaced by the update sequence number; a reader verifies all strides carry the number, then restores the saved bytes.
source: D1 of F3-49 (Linux-NTFS project, "NTFS Documentation" (Richard Russon and Yuval Fledel)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a directory's sorted list of names, as a B-tree.
analogy: the hall's card index, with guide cards that tell you which drawer to open.
precise: the index named $I30 on file names: the root node in $INDEX_ROOT (in the record), further nodes in "INDX" blocks of $INDEX_ALLOCATION, with a $BITMAP of used blocks; entries carry a file reference and a copy of the $FILE_NAME value, and a subnode VCN when they have a child.
source: D1 of F3-49 (Linux-NTFS project, "NTFS Documentation" (Richard Russon and Yuval Fledel)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a spare copy of the first records of the MFT.
analogy: a copy of the register's first forms kept in another room.
precise: the file at record 1 holding copies of at least records 0–3, at a cluster given in the boot sector, used when record 0 cannot be read.
source: D1 of F3-49 (Linux-NTFS project, "NTFS Documentation" (Richard Russon and Yuval Fledel)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a volume that Windows did not finish closing.
analogy: a register left open on the desk with a half-written form.
precise: bit 0x0001 of the volume flags in $Volume's $VOLUME_INFORMATION; metadata may be mid-change, and $LogFile may hold transactions only Windows (or a full log implementation) can replay.
source: D1 of F3-49 (Linux-NTFS project, "NTFS Documentation" (Richard Russon and Yuval Fledel)); D3 of F3-49 (Pavel Yosifovich, Mark Russinovich, Andrea Allievi, Alex Ionescu, David Solomon, "Windows Internals", Part 2, file-system chapter) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)
